name: Vague termination rights or notice periods
description: Contracts using phrases like 'reasonable notice' without defining exact calendar days (e.g., mutually agreed benchmarks such as 30, 60, or 90 days in writing), creating commercial ambiguity and leaving eviction or exit deadlines vulnerable to dispute under contract law.

name: Unclear payment terms or late-payment consequences
description: Agreements lacking defined payment milestones, bank details, grace periods, or containing vague penalty threats like 'landlord/client may take appropriate action' rather than specified liquidated terms.

name: Unilateral price/fee changes
description: Clauses permitting one party to unilaterally increase prices, fees, or charges without requiring bilateral written agreement or signed change-orders.

name: Auto-renewal without clear notice requirements
description: Locking the business into an automatic renewal term unless canceled within a narrow, easily missed notice window, frequently combined with an uncapped rent or rate escalation.

name: Unclear ownership of intellectual property
description: Client pays for custom software or creative deliverables but only receives a limited license or 'right to use', while the vendor retains all underlying copyright and source code ownership.

name: Broad or unclear liability/indemnity clauses
description: One-sided commercial clauses forcing the small business to indemnify the other party for unlimited losses, or capping the counterparty's liability to an ambiguous or negligible amount.

name: Confidentiality and business-data handling not clearly defined
description: Failing to define agreed commercial safeguards regarding the permitted use, protection, return, or secure deletion of proprietary client data, credentials, and customer records upon contract termination.

name: Unclear subcontracting/third-party access
description: Allowing a contractor or vendor to delegate core performance obligations to third-party subcontractors without prior written notice or client approval, diluting confidentiality.

name: Missing scope, deliverables or acceptance criteria
description: Agreements leaving project scope and specifications to be 'discussed later as business needs arise', guaranteeing scope creep, delivery disputes, and uncompensated revisions.

name: Tax/withholding responsibilities not clearly specified
description: Failing to clarify whether agreed amounts are inclusive or exclusive of applicable withholding taxes (such as Section 153 for supplies/services or Section 155 for rent, where the payer is a prescribed withholding agent) and provincial sales tax, risking unexpected payment deductions.
